A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, and their text, tables, figures and equations are readable. v3 includes Supplementary Material, Sections 8–10; the supplied v4 ends after the references without that material. The judgments below concern these supplied documents, not possible external supplements.

before.justification: v3 reports original compression benchmarks across five tasks, cross-task generalization results, runtime measurements and preprocessing ablations, including Tables 3, 6 and 8–11.

after.justification: v4 retains the original five-task compression benchmarks, distortion–accuracy analysis and cross-task generalization results in Tables 3, 5 and 6.

M1.justification: Section 6.1 retains the same truncation, 10-bit quantization, packing, VTM/Hyperprior coding and inverse-processing pipeline. The single-channel Hyperprior adaptation and Equation 1 are unchanged. Omission of supplementary implementation explanations does not establish a method revision.

E1.justification: The five-task evaluation coverage and source datasets in Table 1 are unchanged. However, v3 Table 7 explicitly reports OpenBookQA alongside Arc-Challenge for CSR training; this training-source disclosure disappears in v4. This reduces documented training coverage without establishing that OpenBookQA was actually abandoned or experiments rerun.

E2.justification: Table 3 retains the original-feature reference and the VTM and Hyperprior baselines. Table 6 retains the same Seg-, TTI- and CSR-trained model comparisons. The added related-work citations do not introduce evaluated competitors.

E3.justification: The main benchmark's sample counts, selection rules, metrics, codec settings and truncation ranges remain unchanged. Omitted supplementary analyses remove auxiliary protocols, including truncation sweeps at QPs 27, 32 and 37 and the ten-example sampling and 10-bit/Sobel procedures for feature statistics. Missing training hyperparameters are documentation losses, not demonstrated changes to training.

E4.justification: v4 omits the truncation/quantization ablations, truncation-range sensitivity tests, reconstructed-feature distribution diagnostics and quantitative dataset analyses from v3 Sections 9.3–10, Tables 9–11 and Figures 7–9. These remove substantive tests of preprocessing choices and reconstruction failures. The main generalization experiment in Table 6 remains.

E5.justification: v3 Section 10 and Table 9 report sample-based descriptive statistics, including extrema, means and intensity variance, using ten randomly sampled examples per dataset. This statistical reporting disappears in v4. Neither version reports repeated-run variability, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Main numerical results in Tables 3, 5 and 6 are unchanged, but detailed runtime, feature-statistics and ablation results in Tables 8–11 disappear. For example, v3 Table 10 reports classification accuracy 0 and CSR accuracy 6 for quantization followed by VTM at QP22 without truncation; v4 omits this failure evidence.

T1.justification: Equation 1 and the BPFP and accuracy-drop definitions remain unchanged. Neither version contains theoretical propositions or proofs, and the omitted supplementary material supplies empirical analyses and implementation explanations rather than new formal derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central contributions: a large-model feature dataset, unified test conditions, and two adapted coding baselines with a benchmark. Shortened introductory wording does not materially alter these claims or their scope.

C2.justification: v4 loses substantive supplementary explanations of how truncation mitigates VTM quantization distortion, why Hyperprior rounding can restrict reconstructed feature distributions, and why feature cropping suitable for codec training is unsuitable for large-model training. These mechanisms and applicability qualifications appear in v3 Sections 8.2.1 and 9.3–9.4. Main-text interpretations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Omitting Section 8 and Table 7 removes detailed packing instructions, training-source composition, sample counts, crop dimensions, normalization, epochs, learning rates and lambda values. v4 still directs readers to supplementary details that it does not contain. The code/data pointer also changes from FCM-LM to LaMoFC; external availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v4 adds citations to work on compressed image latents and multimodal LLMs, USTC-TD, segmentation-assisted VVC inter prediction, and VNVC. It removes the Segment Anything citation and associated introductory example. These are limited updates to the literature coverage, without a substantial repositioning of the contribution.

P1.justification: The retained main text receives localized shortening and grammatical edits, particularly in the introduction, background and Section 6 opening. Affiliations, contact information and acknowledgments expand. Sections 1–7 retain their order and narrative; references to supplementary material remain despite its omission.

P2.justification: v4 omits supplementary Tables 7–11 and Figures 6–9, substantially reducing the technical and experimental displays. Main Tables 1–6 and Figures 1–5 retain their content and designs, with limited surrounding text reflow. The removed generalization curves in Figure 6 partly redisplay results still available in Table 6.

improvement.justification: As supplied, v4 preserves the main benchmark but removes reproducibility-critical packing and training specifications, preprocessing ablations and reconstruction diagnostics. This substantially weakens readers' ability to reproduce and assess the baseline design, while retained references still point to the absent supplement. Limited copyediting and additional citations do not compensate for these losses.
